transitions.historical_text: This card can only be Special Summoned by removing 1 EARTH monster in your Graveyard from play. When this card is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard as a result of battle, destroy all Spell and Trap Cards on the field.
transitions.modern_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 EARTH monster in your Graveyard. When this card is destroyed by battle and sent to the Graveyard, destroy all Spell and Trap Cards on the field.
transitions.summary: Wording only. v1 (DR2-EN021) spells out "This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set", which the v0 nomi clause "This card can only be Special Summoned by ..." already imposed, and v2 (CP04-EN015) replaces "destroyed and sent to the Graveyard as a result of battle" with "destroyed by battle and sent to the Graveyard". The summoning restriction and the destruction trigger resolve identically across v0-v2.

transitions.historical_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 EARTH monster in your Graveyard. When this card is destroyed by battle and sent to the Graveyard, destroy all Spell and Trap Cards on the field.
transitions.modern_text: Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set. Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by banishing 1 EARTH monster from your Graveyard. If this card is destroyed by battle and sent to the Graveyard: Destroy all Spell and Trap Cards on the field.
transitions.summary: Wording only, on Konami's period rulings (round 036). The era text "This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 EARTH monster in your Graveyard." says "can only be", not "cannot be Special Summoned except by". Konami's rulebook (Versions 7.0 to 8.0) lets a Special Summon Monster be Special Summoned by another card's effect once it was properly Special Summoned first, and Konami's strategy article (printed 2009-12-07) applies that to "can only be Special Summoned by" wording and keeps the permanent lock for "except by". So the era card and the errata'd "Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by banishing 1 EARTH monster from your Graveyard." revive alike. The errata'd text also pins the proper Summon to the hand, which the era wording leaves unstated; no source read rules on that. No difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

implementation_metadata.reason: Round 036: no generated card was shipped for this record (round 034's script was proposed and never merged; its number 600000010 stays retired). On Konami's period rulings the modern card behaves as the era card did at the snapshots this record applies at, so the modern implementation is used; no script or engine test is needed for it.

Round 036 (2026-09-29) correction. This record's strict-nomi call ("can only be Special Summoned" read as a permanent lock) was read from the printed wording alone and cited no period ruling. Konami's rulebook, Versions 7.0 (capture 2008-12-30), 7.1 (2010-03-30), 7.2 (2011-05-16) and 8.0 (linked from Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18), says of Special Summon Monsters: "You cannot use a card effect to Special Summon those monsters from your hand, Deck, or the Graveyard unless it was properly Special Summoned first." Konami's TCG strategy article (printed date 2009-12-07; earliest capture 2015-11-06) says a monster worded "This card can only be Special Summoned by..." can be Special Summoned again from the Graveyard after one proper Summon, and reserves the permanent lock for "cannot be Special Summoned except by...". Konami's Extreme Victory card rulings (compiled 2011-05-12, version 1.2; listed on Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18) rule, for a card whose text is "This card can only be Special Summoned by controlling 3 or more face-up "Meklord" monsters": "If you Special Summon this card correctly, it can later be Special Summoned back from the Graveyard." This card's text says "can only be" and none of its printed texts says "except", so the era card and the errata'd card revive alike. The Konami OCG card database (cid 5831) says a Gigantes properly Special Summoned can later be Special Summoned from the Graveyard by Monster Reborn; that is OCG evidence and is recorded, not counted. The UDE/Konami card FAQ has no entry for the card. Evidence and its limits: docs/research/period-rulings-generated-scripts.md, sections 3 and 6.9 and the round-036 section. Not established: the Graveyard-revival answer for GOAT (2005-04-01), which is out of this record's scope. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum: the era text is a strict nomi - "This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 EARTH monster in your Graveyard" - so Gigantes can never reach the field by any Special Summon other than its own procedure, and that procedure names no source zone. The errata'd text is semi-nomi, "Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by banishing 1 EARTH monster from your Graveyard", which confines the self-Summon to the hand but lets a Gigantes that was properly Special Summoned once afterwards be Special Summoned by generic means such as Monster Reborn, Premature Burial or Call of the Haunted." Superseded coverage, kept verbatim: "Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode" (gap_sources ignis-babelcdb, yugipedia-card-errata). Superseded gap statement, kept verbatim: "In a period format EDOPro's Gigantes can be revived from the Graveyard by Monster Reborn, Premature Burial or Call of the Haunted once it has been properly Special Summoned, which the era's strict "can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 EARTH monster" text forbids outright."
